packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-17 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

Exposure statement: Nothing in my context proposed an identification of the
work or author. The images themselves carry modern pencil labels on the
lower turn-in reading "Stams, STA, Frg. 92r" (image-007) and
"Stams, STA, Frg. 92v" (image-014); these are shelfmarks, not text
identifications. The working path also contains "stams-c5ugo-batch-5".
Beyond the rules: I ran `ls` on the packet directory (which showed the
file name packet.json; I did not open it), read image sizes with `sips`,
and made three contrast-enhanced enlargements in a scratch directory
(of image-009 col. a top, image-010 right-hand column, image-011 col. b).
All 14 images displayed; no image failed to load.

======================================================================
LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
======================================================================
- Two faces of one opened bifolium used as a binding wrapper; edges turned
  in at top and bottom, corners cut diagonally, a central fold with sewing
  slits. Prick marks in outer margins.
- Face 1 = image-001 (overview), tiles 002-007 (labelled 92r). Face 2 =
  image-008 (overview), tiles 009-014 (labelled 92v).
- Each half-leaf: two columns, ruled; small gothic cursive/textualis
  hybrid, very heavily abbreviated, brown ink. About 22-26 lines per
  column visible.
- Face 2: running title on the upper turn-in above the left page,
  "De confessione" (image-009/010, read as "Deconfessiona"? - the final
  letter is unclear; the reading "De confessione" is likely). A short
  word on the turn-in at far upper left of image-009 ("...ccione"?) is
  cropped by the fold.
- Face 2 left page col. a: several opening lines underlined (009 lines
  2-5); a darker, possibly later or retouched word in line 5 ("Rid'"? /
  "Ricd'"?); marginal notes: in the intercolumn "Am(?)" (009 l.5) and
  "A" + "dicu(n)t?" (009 l.19-20 / 012 l.3-4); in the outer left margin a
  name-like note "Anselm(us)?" / "Ancelm(us)?" (009 l.18 = 012 l.2,
  uncertain reading). Several lines in face-2 right page are also
  underlined (e.g. 013 l.~300 and ~710).
- Face 2 right page: col. a and col. b both full; col. b (image-011/014)
  ends ~4 lines above the column foot. Content (interpretation) is moral/
  homiletic prose on avarice, with numerous biblical citations given by
  book and chapter ("Luc(e) xvi", "xx", etc.).
- Face 1 is badly abraded and faded; the left page col. a is almost
  entirely lost (only ghost traces); left page col. b and right page
  col. a partly legible with darker re-inked-looking words scattered
  among faded ones; right page col. b (image-004) holds only ~9 lines
  at top followed by blank ruled space (end of a section or of the
  text?). Ruled frame lines visible at top of right page col. a (003).
- Marginal letters in outer right margin of face 1 right page
  (image-004): "aprice"?, "vij", "...ovo"?, "meno", "mor"? (cropped/
  faded).

Selected areas: face 2 right page col. a and col. b (most legible),
face 2 left page col. a top, scattered lines of face 1. Largely unread:
face 1 left page col. a (lost), face 1 lower halves, face 2 left page
col. b (only fragments), lower lines of face 2 left page col. a.

Conventions: (x) = expansion; word? = uncertain; [...] = illegible.
Line numbers are counted from the top of the named image, counting text
lines of the column concerned.

======================================================================
TENTATIVE INTERPRETATION (not part of the transcription)
======================================================================
Several visible phrases look like scriptural quotations (my recognition,
not supplied text): 010 a7-9 resembles Ecclus 10 ("amare pecuniam ...
animam suam venalem habet ... proiecit intima sua"); 010 a15 Isa 59
("telas araneae texuerunt"); 013 a7 Col 3 / Eph 5 ("avaritia quae est
idolorum servitus"); 011 b5-8 Eccl 2 ("labore et afflictione spiritus ...
cuncti dies eius laboribus et aerumnis ... nec per noctem ..."); 011 b12
Prov 15 ("conturbat domum suam qui sectatur avaritiam"); 011 b17-18 Luke
16 (dives "sepultus in inferno"). Letters in the transcription were
recorded as seen; uncertain spots remain marked even where these
resemblances suggested a reading.

======================================================================
LIMITATIONS
======================================================================
- Face 1 is severely abraded; most of it is unread. A raking-light or
  UV image would be needed.
- Face 2 left page is faint and very abbreviated; many expansions are
  guesses. Line counts in lower parts of columns are approximate.
- Top lines of face 2 are partly hidden by the folded turn-in and a tear;
  bottom turn-ins hide nothing written but cut the column foot area.
- Tiles overlap: 010/013, 011/014, 009/012 repeat lines; overlaps noted
  above and not counted twice.
- Column order of the bifolium (which half precedes) not determined.
